subsystems.name: Sensor element
subsystems.role: the part that actually measures something — pressure, temperature, vibration, a chemical trace.

subsystems.name: Mote platform
subsystems.role: a complete computer, radio and antenna small enough to be deployed in enormous numbers.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: keeps a node alive for years without maintenance.

subsystems.name: Local collection layer
subsystems.role: gathers data from thousands of nearby motes.

subsystems.name: Space segment
subsystems.role: links remote regions and oceans back to the internet.

subsystems.name: Data pipeline
subsystems.role: turns a firehose of raw readings into calibrated, usable information.

buildSteps.title: Design the mote
buildSteps.detail: Sensor, radio and processor are co-designed so the whole node fits on a few square millimetres and draws microwatts when idle.

buildSteps.title: Solve the power budget
buildSteps.detail: Every reading and transmission is counted in joules; the design balances a tiny battery against harvested energy to give a target service life.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate at wafer scale
buildSteps.detail: MEMS structures are etched from silicon and packaged in the same way as microchips, so the cost per unit falls with volume rather than rising.

buildSteps.title: Build the ground and airborne layer
buildSteps.detail: Gateways, buoys, drones and stratospheric balloons are deployed to carry data out of places with no mobile coverage.

buildSteps.title: Launch the satellite mesh
buildSteps.detail: A constellation in low earth orbit provides backhaul over oceans and deserts, with optical links between satellites.

buildSteps.title: Release or place the nodes
buildSteps.detail: Ground, ocean and infrastructure sensors are installed by hand; any atmospheric version would be dropped from balloons or aircraft, which raises the question of recovering or biodegrading them.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate against references
buildSteps.detail: Cheap sensors drift, so the network must be continuously checked against a small number of accurate reference stations.

buildSteps.title: Fuse and act
buildSteps.detail: Readings are merged into models of the atmosphere, oceans and crust, and thresholds trigger automatic warnings.

prerequisites.why: smart-dust research since the late 1990s showed sensing, computing and radio can fit in a cubic millimetre.
standards such as LoRaWAN show that thousands of battery nodes can share a gateway.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap low-earth-orbit launch and satellite backhaul
prerequisites.why: large constellations exist, but a mesh that can pick up a whisper from a millimetre-scale transmitter does not.
solar and vibration harvesting work, but power density limits how often a node can transmit.
dispersing billions of devices into the air or ocean would otherwise be an environmental problem in itself.

pathway.milestone: existing observatories — a few thousand drifting ocean floats, national seismic networks, weather satellites and early-warning systems
pathway.unlocks: coarse global coverage of climate and earthquakes, with big gaps over oceans and in the developing world.

pathway.milestone: dense regional sensor meshes and cheap satellite backhaul
pathway.unlocks: city-scale and catchment-scale monitoring of air quality, flooding and shaking.
deployment in millions rather than thousands, including on farmland, rivers and ice.

pathway.milestone: a genuinely planet-wide network, likely ground- and ocean-based first
pathway.unlocks: near-real-time digital twin of the planet; airborne dust sensors remain the least plausible and most contested part.
